content.content:
(sysproperty for in-JVM code, environment variable for the fortress
       processes the tests fork), so tracks cannot corrupt each other or
       the tracked default_repository/caches. Per-suite resets are
       disabled: each track starts cold in a fresh directory.
       FORTRESS_THREADS=4 is pinned here, as in systemShard below. Fortress
       runs tuple elements, arguments and for iterations in parallel by
       default, so the tests run in parallel too: a test that fails or
       varies under parallelism is then found, not hidden by one thread.
       The pin makes the thread count a property of this target, the same
       on any machine, and not of the shell that called ant (unpinned, the
       default is half the CPUs).
       JAVA_FLAGS is pinned for the same reason: a compiled test's run step
       is a bin/fortress run process, which takes its heap and stack from
       JAVA_FLAGS, else from bin/run's default with the JVM's 1 MB thread
       stacks.  Above one thread the program runs on the pool's worker
       threads, and library_tests/TimingRungT, whose recursion is 1,000
       calls deep with its operands forked, overflowed such a stack in 8 of
       12 runs at four threads, and in none of 12 with this value, the
       heap and stack that explorations/experiment/env.sh exports. -->
  <macrodef name="fastTrack">
    <attribute name="id"/>
    <element name="tests" implicit="yes"/>
    <sequential>
      <mkdir dir="${test.results}/fast-@{id}"/>
      <junit printsummary="on"
             haltonerror="off"
             haltonfailure="off"
             showoutput="yes"
             fork="true"
             maxmemory="${junitMem}"
             errorProperty="tests.failed"
             failureProperty="tests.failed">
        <classpath refid="compile.classpath"/>
        <sysproperty key="fortress.junit.reset" value="false"/>
        <sysproperty key="fortress.caches" value="${test.caches}/fast-@{id}"/>
        <env key="FORTRESS_CACHES" value="${test.caches}/fast-@{id}"/>
        <env key="FORTRESS_THREADS" value="4"/>
        <env key="JAVA_FLAGS"
             value="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=${basedir}/${PF}/test-tmp"/>
        <jvmarg value="-Djava.io.tmpdir=${PF}/test-tmp" />
        <jvmarg value="${bigStack}" />
        <formatter type="plain" usefile="true"/>
        <batchtest fork="true" todir="${test.results}/fast-@{id}">
          <fileset dir="${build}">
            <tests/>
          </fileset>
        </batchtest>
      </junit>
    </sequential>
  </macrodef>

  <target name="testFast" depends="compileAll"
          description="Run all unit and system tests expected to pass.">
    <mkdir dir="${test.results}"/>
    <mkdir dir="${PF}/test-tmp" />
    <delete quiet="true" dir="${test.caches}"/>
    <!-- The three big suites each dominate a track; everything else shares
         the fourth. Wall clock is the slowest single suite, not the sum. -->
    <parallel threadcount="4">
      <fastTrack id="compiler">
        <include name="**/CompilerJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
      <fastTrack id="library">
        <include name="**/LibraryJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
      <fastTrack id="othercompiler">
        <include name="**/OtherCompilerJUTest.class"/>
      </fastTrack>
      <fastTrack id="misc">
        <include name="**/*JUTest.class"/>
        <include name="**/*JUTests.class"/>
        <exclude name="**/CompilerJUTest.class"/>
        <exclude name="**/LibraryJUTest.class"/>
        <exclude name="**/OtherCompilerJUTest.class"/>

        <!-- Do not run the interpreter tests here. Only run the interpreter
             tests during nightly and CruiseControl testing. -->
        <exclude name="**/TopLevelEnvGenJUTest.class"/>
        <exclude name="**/NightlyCompilerJUTest.class"/>
        <exclude name="**/SpecDataJUTest.class"/>
        <exclude name="**/SystemJUTest.class"/>
        <exclude name="**/*$*.class"/>

component IntLiteralRung6
export Executable

(*) Rung 6 of the compile-path ladder: the comparing operators of IntLiteral
(*) and MIN and MAX, which the compiler world declares and then refuses at
(*) run time.
(*)
(*) A binding written without a declared type from an integer literal keeps
(*) the static type IntLiteral on the compile path, and every operator
(*) applied to it resolves to trait IntLiteral's own declaration rather than
(*) to a coerced ZZ32 or ZZ64 one.  Those declarations exist -- 33 of them,
(*) ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/CompilerBuiltin.fsi:378-410 -- and every
(*) body is "throw CompilerFailureDetectedAtRunTime" (.fss:816-848).  Such a
(*) program therefore compiles clean, links clean, and dies on its first
(*) comparison.  That is gap-ledger row 80.
(*)
(*) The interpreter does not have this trap, and its IntLiteral shows where
(*) the line belongs.  ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/FortressBuiltin.fss:472-481
(*) keeps the comparing family live, with real bodies over cmp; :483-525
(*) comments out the arithmetic family under the note "Do not enable these
(*) until coercion is implemented; doing so will cause all our arithmetic to
(*) occur on IntLiterals."  This rung draws that same line in the compiler
(*) world: bodies for the comparisons, nothing touched in the arithmetic.
(*)
(*) MIN and MAX belong on the comparing side.  The interpreter gets them for
(*) free because its IntLiteral extends ZZ32; the compiler world's extends
(*) Number and Equality only, so they need bodies of their own, and they can
(*) have them, because each returns one of its two operands and so needs no
(*) way to build a new IntLiteral.  That is exactly what separates this rung
(*) from the arithmetic family, whose results are new values.
tests=IntLiteralRung6
link
run

content.content:
(* The static numerals: a negative constant through the type's own minus, a generic program type, a static expression through a coercion from QQ, the defaults, and no numeral value at run time. *)
component NumeralStaticDesignWalk
import Reflect.{ typeOf }
export Executable

oneRounding(v: ZZ, r: ZZ32, m: ZZ32): RR64 =
    builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleDoubleArith.numeralToDouble")

value object CC64(re: RR64, im: RR64)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = CC64(oneRounding(v, r.asZZ32, 0), 0.0)
    coerce[\nat n, nat m, nat r, nat v\](x: RadixPointNumeral[\n, m, r, v\]) =
        CC64(oneRounding(v, r.asZZ32, m.asZZ32), 0.0)
    opr -(self): CC64 = CC64(-re, -im)
    opr +(self, other: CC64): CC64 = CC64(re + other.re, im + other.im)
    opr -(self, other: CC64): CC64 = CC64(re - other.re, im - other.im)
    opr juxtaposition(self, other: CC64): CC64 =
        CC64(re other.re - im other.im, re other.im + im other.re)
end

i: CC64 = CC64(0.0, 1.0)

value object Tally(k: ZZ32, seen: ZZ, negated: Boolean)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = Tally(v.asZZ32, v, false)
    opr -(self): Tally = Tally(-k, seen, true)
end

object Gen[\T\](v: ZZ)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = Gen[\T\](v)
end

site(): Gen[\RR64\] = 3

value object Half(lo: QQ)
    coerce(q: QQ) = Half(q)
end

object Cell[\T\](c: T) end

value object Byte(b: ZZ32)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) where { v < 256 } = Byte(v.asZZ32)
end

isZZ32(a: Any): Boolean = typecase a of ZZ32 => true; else => false end
isCellZZ32(a: Any): Boolean = typecase a of Cell[\ZZ32\] => true; else => false end

run(): () = do
    t: Tally = -3
    assert(t.k, -3, "-3 at Tally is Tally's minus on the coercion of 3")
    assert(t.seen, big(3), "the coercion sees the written numeral 3, without its sign")
    assert(t.negated, "Tally's own minus ran on -3")
    c: CC64 = -3 - 4 i
    assert(c.re SEQV -3.0, "-3 - 4 i has the real part -3.0")
    assert(c.im SEQV -4.0, "-3 - 4 i has the imaginary part -4.0")
    c3: CC64 = -3.5
    assert((c3.re SEQV -3.5) AND (c3.im SEQV -0.0), "-3.5 at CC64 is CC64's minus on the coercion of 3.5")
    z: ZZ32 = -2147483648
    assert(z + 2147483647, -1, "-2147483648 at ZZ32 folds exactly, then converts")
    r: RR64 = -0.0
    assert(r.rawBits, -9223372036854775808, "-0.0 at RR64 is IEEE's negative zero")
    assert((1/r).isInfinite AND (1/r) < 0, "1/r is -Infinity for r: RR64 = -0.0")
    assert(site() SEQV site(), "a numeral at a program's generic type is one object per place")
    g1: Gen[\RR64\] = 3
    g2: Gen[\RR64\] = 3
    assert(NOT (g1 SEQV g2), "two places at a program's generic type give two objects")
    assert(g1.v, big(3), "g: Gen of RR64 = 3 sees the value 3")
    h: Half = 10/20
    assert(h.lo = 1/2, "10/20 at a type with a coercion from QQ reaches it as the QQ 1/2")
    assert(0.1_2 SEQV 0.5, "0.1_2 SEQV 0.5")
    assert(NOT (0.1 = 0.1_16), "0.1 = 0.1_16 is false")
    q: QQ = 0.1
    assert(numerator(q), big(1), "q: QQ = 0.1 is exactly 1/10")
    assert(denominator(q), big(10), "q: QQ = 0.1 is exactly 1/10")
    f: RR64 = 0.1
    assert(f.rawBits, 4591870180066957722, "f: RR64 = 0.1 rounds once")
    y: Byte = 255
    assert(y.b, 255, "255 at a byte type whose coercion holds v < 256")
    x = 3
    assert(isZZ32(x), "x = 3 is a ZZ32")
    assert(isCellZZ32(Cell(3)), "Cell(3) is a Cell of ZZ32")
    assert(typeOf(3).asString, "ZZ32", "typeOf(3) shows no numeral type")
    assert(typeOf(0.5).asString, "RR64", "typeOf(0.5) shows no numeral type")
    println "PASS"
  end

end

(* A numeral as written at each integer type of the library converts there exactly from its value, at the type's bounds and beyond 64 bits at ZZ. *)
component NumeralFoldIntegers
export Executable

run(): () = do
    a: ZZ32 = 2147483647
    a0: ZZ32 = 0
    b: NN32 = 4294967295
    b0: NN32 = 0
    c: ZZ64 = 9223372036854775807
    d: NN64 = 18446744073709551615
    e: ZZ = 123456789012345678901234567890
    println(a)
    println(a0)
    println(b)
    println(b0)
    println(c)
    println(d)
    println(e)
end

end
EOF
cat > NumeralFoldIntegers.test <<'EOF'
tests=NumeralFoldIntegers
link
run
run_out_equals=2147483647\n0\n4294967295\n0\n9223372036854775807\n18446744073709551615\n123456789012345678901234567890\n
EOF
cat > NumeralFoldFloats.fss <<'EOF'
(* A numeral as written at RR64 and RR32 converts there from its exact value by one rounding, its bits those of the nearest float, more than 20 digits included. *)
component NumeralFoldFloats
export Executable

rawBits(x: RR64): ZZ64 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleDoubleArith.doubleRawBits")
floatBits(x: RR32): ZZ32 = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.simpleFloatArith.floatRawBits")

run(): () = do
    f: RR64 = 0.1
    g: RR32 = 0.1
    h: RR32 = 16777217.0
    k: RR64 = 0.1_2
    p: RR64 = 3.1415926535897932384626
    q: RR32 = 1.00000005960464477539063
    println(rawBits(f))
    println(floatBits(g))
    println(h)
    println(k)
    println(rawBits(p))
    println(floatBits(q))
end

end
EOF
cat > NumeralFoldFloats.test <<'EOF'
tests=NumeralFoldFloats
link
run
run_out_equals=4591870180066957722\n1036831949\n1.6777216E7\n0.5\n4614256656552045848\n1065353217\n
EOF
python3 - <<'PY'
import struct
from fractions import Fraction
# nearest double to pi to 22 digits, and nearest float to 1.00000005960464477539063
x = float(Fraction("3.1415926535897932384626"))
print(struct.unpack('<q', struct.pack('<d', x))[0])
fr = Fraction("1.00000005960464477539063")
# round to float32 by hand: ulp at 1.0 is 2^-23
ulp = Fraction(1, 2**23)
k = fr / ulp
lo = int(k); rem = k - lo
k2 = lo + (1 if rem > Fraction(1,2) or (rem == Fraction(1,2) and lo % 2 == 1) else 0)
val = k2 * ulp
print(k2, float(val), struct.unpack('<i', struct.pack('<f', float(val)))[0])
PY

(* The api of NumeralAcrossComponent: a number type of a program whose numeral coercion its component declares. *)
api NumeralAcrossComponentApi

object Wide(z: ZZ)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\])
end

end
EOF
cat > NumeralAcrossComponentApi.fss <<'EOF'
(* The component of the api NumeralAcrossComponentApi: the coercion calls a function that the component does not export. *)
component NumeralAcrossComponentApi
export NumeralAcrossComponentApi

object Wide(z: ZZ)
    coerce[\nat n, nat r, nat v\](x: NaturalNumeral[\n, r, v\]) = do
        println("wide")
        Wide(kept(v))
    end
end

kept(z: ZZ): ZZ = z

end
EOF
cat > NumeralAcrossComponent.fss <<'EOF'
(* A numeral at a program's type whose coercion another component declares is one object for its place, made once by that component's compiled coercion, a numeral of more than 20 digits included. *)
component NumeralAcrossComponent
import NumeralAcrossComponentApi.{...}
export Executable

sEq(a: Any, b: Any): Boolean = builtinPrimitive("com.sun.fortress.nativeHelpers.equality.sEquiv")

three(): Wide = 3
four(): Wide = 4
huge(): Wide = 123456789012345678901234567890

run(): () = do
    println("start")
    a = three()
    b = three()
    c = four()
    assert(sEq(a, b), "two evaluations of one place are one object")
    assert(NOT sEq(a, c), "two places are two objects")
    println(a.z)
    println(c.z)
    println(huge().z)
    assert(sEq(huge(), huge()), "the place of a numeral of more than 20 digits is one object")
    println("PASS")
end

end
EOF
cat > NumeralAcrossComponent.test <<'EOF'
tests=NumeralAcrossComponent
link
run
run_out_equals=wide\nwide\nwide\nstart\n3\n4\n123456789012345678901234567890\nPASS\n
EOF
ls NumeralAcross*

    assert(sEq(a, b), "two evaluations of the place of -3 are one object")

    println("PASS")
end

end
EOF
